source.title: On Avoiding Local Minima Using Gradient Descent With Large Learning Rates
source.authors: Amirkeivan Mohtashami; Martin Jaggi; Sebastian U. Stich

record.file_problem: The full text is present. Its title, “Special Properties of Gradient Descent with Large Learning Rates,” differs from the supplied title.
record.tranche_reason: The paper compares training outcomes under different learning-rate recipes on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, bearing on V1, but it does not use the claim’s criterion of zero or near-zero training classification error as an explicitly reported numerical result.
record.gate_note: The paper reports train-accuracy curves in figures for the learning-rate comparisons. The cited CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 values are figure-only; no exact train-accuracy values are stated in the text. Toy-function convergence rates and theoretical results are not rows for the listed versions.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 training-accuracy results for ResNet-18 under different learning-rate and batch-repeat recipes, bearing on V1 in a new training setting. The supplied text does not preserve readable curve endpoints, so near-zero training error cannot be established.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors argue that large learning rates affect optimization beyond amplifying stochastic noise, supported by batch-repeat experiments and theory for constrained function classes. Their warm-started neural-network experiment provides evidence consistent with escaping a sharp region, rather than definitively identifying and verifying escape from a local minimum.
record.recipe_differences: The CIFAR experiments compare learning rates and batch repeats, rather than testing the claim’s random-initialization and zero-training-error recipe. The network is a ResNet-18 without batch normalization in the main experiment; the large-versus-small trajectory comparison warm-starts from SGD.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported performance gap depends on learning rate and batch repeats; on CIFAR-10 without momentum or weight decay, repeats do not improve results.

fits_no_version.finding: Warm-started full-batch ResNet-18 training at learning rate 0.01 shows an initial loss spike and a different subsequent trajectory from training at 0.001.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Large learning rates can produce transient loss increases and change the optimization trajectory after a small-learning-rate warm start.

fits_no_version.finding: For specially constructed nonconvex functions, the authors prove that sufficiently large steps escape sharp local minima and converge under additional landscape assumptions; toy experiments illustrate escape and avoidance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Above-threshold gradient descent can escape local minima and converge on particular nonconvex function classes.

fits_no_version.finding: Increasing stochasticity through batch repeats does not close the performance gap between small and large learning rates; without momentum and weight decay, repeats provide no observed improvement.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The benefits of large learning rates in these ResNet-18 experiments cannot be reproduced fully by the tested batch-repeat procedure.

record.problems: The train-accuracy results are shown in figures without exact values stated in the text. The main comparison averages 3 runs; uncertainty estimates are not stated. The trajectory experiment warm-starts the network, so it does not establish behavior from random initialization.
record.rows_left_out: No result rows omitted. Toy-function convergence results and theoretical bounds were not included because they do not measure a listed version’s CIFAR or model training-error outcome.

untested.parts: Random or corrupted labels, model-size scaling, smaller-model exceptions, early-stopping comparisons, and initialization dependence are not tested. Random initialization is not explicitly documented for these neural-network experiments.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student experiment or student-width comparison.
No depth comparison or comparison of plain networks with identity shortcuts.
No comparison of initialization schemes, signal propagation, or trainable depth.

No neural-network measurement of the initial linearized stability limit, curvature reduction, sharpness tracking at the stability threshold, or divergence across a learning-rate sweep. The warm-started loss spike alone does not test these mechanisms.
No comparison with batch normalization or Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: No verdict label is justified from the supplied training-accuracy values: figure axes and legends survive text extraction, but the curves do not. Lower relative performance alone cannot establish substantial training error. References to edge-of-stability sharpness measurements describe prior work, not measurements made in this study.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test random or corrupted labels, model-size scaling, smaller models, or early stopping. The CIFAR-10 experiment uses a ResNet-18 without batch normalization; initialization is not stated. It reports train-accuracy curves but does not state exact values or explicitly report zero or near-zero training classification error.
The paper studies large learning rates and loss increases, but does not report the specified stability-limit, curvature-drop, or sharpness-threshold measurements.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Compared standard SGD at learning rate 0.01 with standard SGD at 0.001 and SGD with 10 batch repeats at 0.001.
rows.note: The figure contains separate curves for the three recipes; the text says the 0.01 recipe leads to a much better model and repeats reduce, but do not close, the performance gap. Exact train-accuracy values are not stated.
rows.check: Split the three recipes into separate rows. Include absence of batch normalization, momentum 0.9, weight decay 0.0005, learning-rate decays, and the different training durations. The qualitative performance comparison does not establish which recipes reach near-zero training error; curve endpoints are unavailable in the supplied text.
